newsitem.title: USA: US Treasuries close down amid dearth of releases.
newsitem.headline: US Treasuries close down amid dearth of releases.

text.p: U.S. Treasury securities prices closed lower on Thursday as players had little new information to trade on ahead of a long holiday in the U.S.
Hedge fund selling dominated trade as players unwound positions and the dollar weakened.
The only important economic data released on Thursday was initial unemployment claims, which rose 5,000 from the prior week. That produced little reaction from the bond market.
The bond market was scheduled to close early on Friday at 1400 EDT/1800 GMT.
Initial unemployment claims were reported at 322,000 in the week ended May 17, a 5,000 increase. But that figure had little impact on Treasuries prices.

Instead, economists said, hedge fund selling continued in a curve flattening enviroment following the Federal Reserve's failure to hike short-term interest rates at its policy-making arm's meeting on Tuesday.
"There's still some nervousness on selling in the futures. Nobody's going to be willing to take the upper side going into the long weekend," said Jerry Zukowski, economist at PaineWebber Inc.
Zukowski said retail sales were very slim, even as trading volume was above average, according to GovPX.

"It's talking heads version 1,000 as the data come in. Everybody seems to be making up their mind (about another tightening of short-term interest rates by the Federal Reserve on July 2), but it looks like (the Fed) is watching the data," Zukowski said.

Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan has stated he would favor further tightening should the U.S. economy continue to show robust growth, even if there were no obvious signals of inflation from economic indicators.

The Fed released minutes on Thursday afternoon from its March 25 meeting -- when it tightened the federal funds rate by 25 basis points -- indicating that it had adopted a neutral bias regarding monetary policy.
"The market seemed to jump on news they moved to a neutral policy directive and that it had long-term policy implications," said Douglas Schindewolf, money market economist at Smith Barney Inc.
However, Schindewolf pointed out that the minutes implied that the Fed had only adopted a neutral bias for an intermeeting period.
Schindewolf said market reaction that the Fed would move only once was incorrect.
But with a lack of economic data releases the rest of the week the market wasn't likely to make any significant moves before the three-day Memorial Day holiday in the U.S., analysts said.
Schindewolf said there was large amount of hedge fund selling, affecting price movement throughout the session.

The 30-year bond was down 10/32 at 95-15/32 to yield 6.99 percent. The 10-year note closed at 99-3/32, down 5/32 to yield 6.75 percent. Five-year notes ended at 100-5/32, down 3/32 to yield 6.59 percent.
Near the shorter end of the maturity range, two-year notes closed at 100-8/32, off 1/32 to yield 6.23 percent.
Three-month bill rates rose five basis points to 5.03 percent. Six-month bill rates rose one basis point to 5.23 percent. Year bill rates were up one basis point at 5.48 percent.
